{{short description|Mozambican chemist and politician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2020}}
'''Iolanda Maria Pedro Campos Cintura Seuane''' (born 24 October 1972{{cn|date=October 2025}}) is a [[Demographics of Mozambique|Mozambican]] [[chemist]] and politician who served as Minister for Women and Social Affairs from 2010 to 2014 and has been governor of the capital city [[Maputo]] since 2015.

==Early life and education==
Cintura was born on 24 October 1972 in Vila Pery (now [[Chimoio]]), [[Manica Province]]. She attended primary school in [[Beira, Mozambique|Beira]] before moving to Maputo for her secondary schooling. She studied chemistry at [[Eduardo Mondlane University]], graduating in 1999. She also received certificates in fuel management from the [[Norwegian Petroleum Institute]] (1999), energy relations from the [[United States Department of Energy]] (2001) and management from the [[Pedagogical University]] of Maputo (2007 and 2011).<ref name=bio/>

==Career==
Cintura is a member of the [[Mozambique Liberation Front]] and held various positions in the Ministry of Energy from 2000 until 2010.<ref name=bio/> On 15 January 2010, she was appointed to the cabinet by [[List of heads of state of Mozambique|President]] [[Armando Guebuza]] as Minister for Women and Social Affairs.<ref>{{cite book|page=88|title=A Decade of Mozambique: Politics, Economy and Society 2004–2013|first=Joseph|last=Hanlon|publisher=Brill|year=2015}}</ref> In this capacity, she made a statement to the [[United Nations Commission on the Status of Women]] in New York City in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.un.org/womenwatch/daw/csw/csw56/general-discussions/member-states/Mozambique.pdf|title=Statement by the Honourable Iolanda Cintura Minister of Woman and Social Action of the Republic of Mozambique|date=February 2012|publisher=[[UN Women]]}}</ref> In April 2013, she hosted the [[Southern African Development Community]]'s meeting of ministers responsible for gender and women's affairs in Maputo.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sadc.int/news-events/news/sadc-ministers-condemn-violence-against-women-and-girls/|publisher=Southern African Development Community|title=SADC Ministers Condemn Violence Against Women and Girls|date=3 April 2013|accessdate=12 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nation.sc/article.html?id=237662|work=Seychelles Nation|title=Seychelles at SADC gender and women ministers’ meeting|date=1 March 2013|accessdate=12 March 2017}}</ref>

After the [[2014 Mozambican general election|2014 presidential election]], [[Filipe Nyusi]] did not keep Cintura in the cabinet, but in January 2015 appointed her as governor of Maputo.<ref>{{cite web|language=Portuguese|url=http://opais.sapo.mz/index.php/politica/63-politica/33879-iolanda-cintura-apresentada-como-governadora-.html|title=Iolanda Cintura apresentada como Governadora|date=23 January 2015|accessdate=12 March 2017|work=O Pais|archive-date=14 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190714030718/http://opais.sapo.mz/index.php/politica/63-politica/33879-iolanda-cintura-apresentada-como-governadora-.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.miramar.co.mz/Noticias/Iolanda-Cintura-visita-a-Direccao-de-Plano-e-Financas|language=Portuguese|title=Iolanda Cintura visita a Direcção de Plano e Finanças|publisher=Miramar|date=16 September 2015|accessdate=12 March 2017|archive-date=12 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312200259/http://www.miramar.co.mz/Noticias/Iolanda-Cintura-visita-a-Direccao-de-Plano-e-Financas|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://clubofmozambique.com/news/governor-calls-expansion-specialist-surgical-services-reduce-waiting-times-maputo-health-units/|title=Governor calls for expansion of specialist and surgical services to reduce waiting times in Maputo health units|date=9 February 2017|accessdate=12 March 2017|work=Club of Mozambique|first=Adrian|last=Frey}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://allafrica.com/stories/201501200312.html|title=Mozambique: President Nyusi Appoints Provincial Governors|date=19 January 2015|accessdate=12 March 2017|publisher= All Africa}}</ref>

Cintura has been a member of the National AIDS Council since 2010 and is president of the National Council for the Advancement of Women.{{cn|date=October 2025}}

==Personal life==
Cintura is married to Mário Seuane and has two children.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.biografia.co.mz/index.php/pt/politica/111-biografia-de-iolanda-cintura|language=Portuguese|title=Notas biográficas de Iolanda Cintura|first=Dalton|last=Sitoe|date=8 April 2016|accessdate=12 March 2017|work=Biografia}}</ref>
